newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cricket-West Indies show more unified front.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cricket-West Indies show more unified front.

text.p: West Indies, whose last visit was marred by internal conflict and poor results, are presenting a more unified appearance before the first test against Australia, starting in Brisbane on Friday.
There are growing signs of unity as the tourists seek to avenge their series defeat against Mark Taylor's men in the Caribbean in May last year, according to recent opponents.
"There has been a bit of conflict in the team in previous years but I think they are all right behind Courtney Walsh as captain," Western Australia wicketkeeper and captain Adam Gilchrist said.
"Their team spirit is good -- they seem to be keen to work for one another," said Gilchrist, whose state side slumped to defeat inside three days against West Indies ten days ago.
With former captain Richie Richardson at the helm, West Indies endured a dismal short tour of Australia last December and January, prompting media reports of dressing room disharmony.

West Indies failed to reach the final of a triangular tournament in Australia last January. In several tour matches they gave the impression of a team in disarray and under siege, falling to defeat with barely any resistance.
They then fell at the semifinal stage at this year's World Cup, a failure highlighted by a shock loss to minnows Kenya.
Those results led to Richardson's resignation as captain and the sackings of coach Andy Roberts and manager Wes Hall.
The current West Indies are being led by veteran fast bowler Walsh, manager Clive Lloyd and coach Malcolm Marshall.

West Indies have enjoyed mixed results in first-class matches so far on tour. After beating Western Australia, they fielded a second-string bowling attack against an Australia XI and slumped to a 10-wicket defeat on Monday.
